breaking.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over China chip fears as probes pile up
breaking.fact: Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia Thursday, asking whether its advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether the company misled investors about the risk. The state probe lands on top of the SEC's accounting investigation, with Jensen Huang due before three House committees on Dec. 1.

breaking.headline: Fed's Cook doubles down: policy 'isn't restrictive enough' to curb inflation
breaking.fact: Governor Lisa Cook said Friday that September's rate hike did too little and warned that waiting could make inflation — above target for 67 months — harder to dislodge, standing by her October dissent for a hike. Her remarks kept December hike pricing near certain even as stocks slid into the close.

breaking.headline: Flight to safety pulls the 10-year Treasury yield back below 5%
breaking.fact: Treasuries rallied hard Friday as investors fled the equity rout, dragging the 10-year yield down to about 4.92% — roughly 23 basis points lower over five sessions — even as Fed officials talked tough on inflation. The 2-year yield fell 13 basis points on the day as the curve steepened.
breaking.source: T. Rowe Price Global Markets Weekly (Reuters data)

breaking.headline: Gold's rout deepens: the metal closes a brutal week at $3,535, down 9%
breaking.fact: Gold settled Friday at $3,535.20 an ounce, capping a 9.03% weekly plunge, while silver cratered 16.27% to $41.06 and copper slid 10.12%. Hawkish Fed talk and a firm dollar left the week's 'sell everything' trade with few hiding places, precious metals included.
breaking.source: Weekly market report (Yahoo Finance / exchange settlements)

weekInBrief.headline: Nasdaq 100 posts its worst week since March 2020
weekInBrief.body: The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% Friday and 10.4% for the week — its deepest weekly drop since the pandemic crash — as the AI trade unwound. The Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026 and slipped into bear-market territory, more than 20% below its Oct. 6 record close.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran as military warns of strain, FT reports
weekInBrief.body: President Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran, the Financial Times reported, even as U.S. military officials warn that months of operations have strained forces and munitions stockpiles. The deliberations come with Gulf export flows back near prewar levels and crude posting its third straight weekly decline.

weekInBrief.headline: Dollar index climbs toward multi-month highs near 104
weekInBrief.body: The dollar rallied through the week as traders priced in near-certain further Fed tightening, pushing the DXY toward 104 — around its strongest levels in months. The firm greenback added to the pressure on gold, silver and industrial metals, which all posted steep weekly losses.

weekInBrief.headline: Natural gas jumps 17% on the week as early cold arrives
weekInBrief.body: U.S. natural gas futures settled Friday at $3.79 per MMBtu, up about 17% for the week — a rare gainer in a 'sell everything' market — as early-season cold across the Midwest and Northeast lifted heating demand. The move stood out against crude oil's third straight weekly decline.

weekendStories.headline: Houston Restaurant Weeks serves up a $2 million check for the Food Bank
weekendStories.body: Houston's restaurants — and the diners who packed them — turned a season of prix-fixe meals into a $2,012,076 donation to the Houston Food Bank, enough for more than six million meals. It was the biggest year in the event's history, pushing the 23-year total past $25 million raised for neighbors facing food insecurity.

weekendStories.headline: Houston volunteers bring 2,500 pounds of food — and thanks — to veterans at Camp Hope
weekendStories.body: Fifth graders from DAV Montessori joined Sewa International volunteers on Nov. 18 to deliver roughly 2,500 pounds of food to Camp Hope, the PTSD Foundation of America's Houston recovery home for veterans. The kids carried a handmade 'Thank You' poster, and the visit capped a Sewa Diwali drive that has gathered more than 30,000 pounds of food across Greater Houston this season.

weekendStories.headline: Plains students honor Sanders County veterans with ceremony and luncheon
weekendStories.body: On a foggy Veterans Day morning, ten veterans from Plains VFW Post 3596 gathered at Plains Cemetery while local students led the remembrance — then National Honor Society members served 18 veterans a luncheon at the high school. It's the fifth year Plains teacher Charity Jermyn has paired her students with the county's veterans for the day.

weekendStories.headline: Bison keep rolling: NDSU beats Hawai'i 21-13 for its eighth win
weekendStories.body: North Dakota State improved to 8-2 with a 21-13 road win over the Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors on Saturday night, its second straight victory. The Bison sit second in the Mountain West and are a perfect 5-0 at home heading into this Saturday's matchup with Northern Illinois.

weekendStories.headline: Pow wow at the Soo honors Native culture and Indigenous veterans
weekendStories.body: Tribal communities gathered at Kewadin Casinos in Sault Ste. Marie on Nov. 14 for a Native American Heritage Month pow wow co-hosted by Bay Mills Community College and the Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians. With grand entries, drum groups and dance specials, the free celebration put a special focus on honoring Indigenous veterans just days after Veterans Day.

weekendStories.headline: Isaac the cat, found hiding in the rubble, is back with his girl
weekendStories.body: Days after a Brooklyn building collapse killed eight people, 13-year-old Zariah Coleman pleaded at a news conference for help finding her cat. A Flatbush Cats rescuer searched the damaged apartment three times before hearing a soft meow from a cabinet under the kitchen sink — Isaac, hungry and frightened but alive, is recovering and reunited with his family.

weekendStories.headline: Four cousins turn a family Thanksgiving game into gifts for sick kids
weekendStories.body: Two Houston cousins and their two Scarsdale, N.Y. cousins built 'Thoughtful Turkey' — a plush toy, storybook and gratitude-card kit — out of their family's longtime Thanksgiving tradition. Since launching Oct. 1 they have sold more than 200 kits and donated over 150, including 20 to children in the bone marrow transplant unit at Texas Children's Hospital.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A tanker sailing outbound through the strait was struck by an unidentified projectile Friday about 8 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, catching fire with no casualties reported, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations (Warning 214-26); Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the vessel hit a naval mine, a claim not independently verified. Iran has also positioned more than 14 tankers at Kharg Island in a convoy to test the U.S. blockade, with crews assigned and flags raised, according to TankerTrackers and satellite imagery, while U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Thursday that energy flows through the strait were increasing. On oil, the roughly 200,000 barrels transferred Tuesday has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil and products kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Flight 17's Ship 44 and Booster 24 reunite at Massey's for cryo testing
space.body: Less than a week after Flight 15's historic orbital catch, both of Flight 17's vehicles — Ship 44 and Booster 24 — are together at SpaceX's Massey's test site in Texas for cryogenic proof testing. Elon Musk says the caught Ship 42 may go on public display rather than fly again, and speculation is building over whether Flight 16 or Flight 17 takes the first Starship launch from Kennedy's Pad 39A.

space.headline: Astronomers watch a puffy dying star swallow its companion whole
space.body: For the first time, astronomers have directly watched a giant star engulf a smaller companion: a supergiant seven times the sun's mass and 18,000 times brighter ballooned to 350 times the sun's width before the pair merged in an eruption a million times brighter than the sun. The merged star, nicknamed 'Bao,' may have been rejuvenated by the meal, the researchers report in Nature.

space.headline: Runny ancient lava rewrites the story of Mars's Jezero Crater floor
space.body: Perseverance rover data show the Séítah formation at the bottom of Jezero Crater formed from an unusually low-viscosity lava that flowed some 124 miles from its vent and pooled like a lava lake nearly 4 billion years ago. The finding, published in Communications Earth & Environment, sharpens the picture of early Mars — and of the very terrain the rover is sampling for signs of ancient life.

space.headline: New satellite dataset extends NASA's ozone record into a new era
space.body: NASA Goddard researchers have built a global ozone dataset from the NOAA-20 satellite that matches the existing record to within about half a Dobson unit, extending decades of ozone monitoring into the JPSS era. That continuity is how scientists track the stratospheric ozone layer's slow recovery year by year.

apod.title: Scotland's Flow Country
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey — NASA Earth Observatory Image of the Day, November 12, 2026
apod.explanation: The blanket bogs of northern Scotland look unassuming — soggy, treeless country of moss, grass and heather — but they are carbon vaults: waterlogged soils keep dead plants from fully decaying, so peat has piled up for more than 9,000 years, in places over eight meters thick. This Landsat 8 view centers on Europe's largest blanket bog, the first peatland ever named a UNESCO World Heritage Site; worldwide, peatlands cover just 3 percent of land yet store more carbon than all the world's forests combined.
